source: USGS 3DEP ND_SouthWest_2021_D21 (work unit ND_SouthWest_1_D21), tile 13tfn040320 extent, read from the public EPT copy (s3 usgs-lidar-public); acquired 2021-11-06 (leaf-off), QL2
tiers:
Assign tiers/labels and interpretations, write candidates.json.
Tier A: compact (L/W<=3), open ground (canopy<3 m), off scarp (10 m context slope<=3.5°), depth/height >=0.15/0.18 m.
Tier B: house-adjacent features failing one Tier-A test, and linear features >=15 m long on the terrace (context<=3.5°).
Tier C: everything else that passed the significance screen (mostly floodplain scroll/gully/cottonwood root forms).

candidates.label: M1
candidates.interpretation: Low ridge (0.22 m, 5x3 m) inside SE part of footprint. Could be collapsed sill/foundation fill or chimney-base rubble; equally could be root mound of the adjacent trees. Low confidence.

candidates.label: M2
candidates.interpretation: Small compact mound 0.23 m high, 3.6 m across, 4 m E of D2 -- possibly spoil from D2 or a collapsed chimney/rubble heap. Low-moderate.

candidates.label: M3
candidates.interpretation: Low elongated rise (0.18 m, 5x2 m) 12.6 m NW of house; together with M2 forms a short NW-SE ridge west of the house. Possible spoil/rubble, low confidence.

candidates.label: D2
candidates.interpretation: Strongest single anomaly. Round, steep-walled pit ~2.5-2.7 m across, 0.35-0.45 m deep, ringed by a 0.1-0.15 m raised rim in 10 of 12 sectors (spoil ring) -- the highest ring score anywhere in the 300 m tile and absent from background windows. Open grass, no tree (only a small shrub in it). 16 m W of house center (rear of house). Best match for a settled/backfilled hand-dug well, privy or cache/root pit. Natural alternatives (badger den, collapsed burrow) usually leave spoil on one side only. Moderate-high confidence that it is anthropogenic; function unknown.

candidates.label: D3
candidates.interpretation: Broad shallow E-W hollow (~10x5 m, 0.23 m) 19 m N of house, bounded on the north by a sharp 0.6-0.8 m rise to the knoll. Sits on the bare trail junction seen in imagery. Could be a structure hollow (cow shed/ outbuilding pad), but trail trampling and natural knoll-foot swale are likely. Low-moderate.

candidates.label: D4
candidates.interpretation: Shallow pit (0.17 m, 3.8x1.9 m) 22 m SE of house, paired 5 m W of mound M4. A pit+mound pair SE of the house is the right position for the blacksmith shop (forge base/slag mound) but the evidence is weak; it is beside the main access trail.

candidates.label: D5
candidates.interpretation: Small pit (2.9x1.6 m, 0.18 m) 24 m NW, open ground. Unknown; possible animal wallow/burrow or small cultural pit. Low.

candidates.label: D6
candidates.interpretation: Small pit (3x1.6 m, 0.19 m) 25 m S, at tree edge (2.5 m shrub). Possible tree-throw/stump hollow. Low.

candidates.label: D7
candidates.interpretation: Small hollow (2.2x1.3 m, 0.17 m) on scarp top 25 m ESE. Not a bank notch. Low.

candidates.label: M4
candidates.interpretation: Compact mound 0.22 m high, ~6x3 m, 26 m SE (136 deg) on the terrace edge. Candidate for blacksmith-shop debris/forge base given position SE of house; could equally be a cottonwood root mound or natural levee knob. Low-moderate.

candidates.label: M5
candidates.interpretation: Mound 0.21 m, 5x3.5 m, 28 m NW, open ground. Unknown; low.

candidates.label: M6
candidates.interpretation: Crest of the natural knoll N of the house (top ~649.6 m). Natural.

candidates.label: D8
candidates.interpretation: Shallow irregular hollow (6x3 m, 0.15 m) 33 m NW. Unknown, low.

candidates.label: D9
candidates.interpretation: Small hollow (3.7x2 m, 0.17 m) 33 m SSE near trail/scarp top. Low.

candidates.label: M7
candidates.interpretation: Small mound 36 m NNW on knoll flank. Natural/unknown.

candidates.label: D10
candidates.interpretation: Trough along the toe of the NE scarp (5x2.4 m, 0.17 m) where the NNE trail runs; scarp-foot swale/trail. Not a dugout notch. Natural/trail.

candidates.label: M8
candidates.interpretation: Elongated mound 37 m NW on knoll edge; natural micro-relief likely.

candidates.label: M9
candidates.interpretation: Small mound 38 m WNW; unknown, low.

candidates.label: D11
candidates.interpretation: Small hollow 40 m N beside NNW trail; trail wear or natural. Low.

candidates.label: D12
candidates.interpretation: Hollow at scarp toe 41 m NNE beside trail. Natural/trail.

candidates.label: M10
candidates.interpretation: Mound 49 m SSE beside access trail; possibly cottonwood root mound. Low.

candidates.label: D13
candidates.interpretation: Second-largest closed depression: 9x7 m, 0.32 m deep, 50 m NNW on open flat terrace (246 ground pts, no canopy), just west of the NNW trail. Size fits a small structure hollow, stock pond/wallow or borrow pit; a natural swale is also possible. Low-moderate; worth a field look.

candidates.label: M11
candidates.interpretation: Mound 60 m S near access trail. Low.

candidates.label: M12
candidates.interpretation: Mound 64 m NNW. Low.

candidates.label: M13
candidates.interpretation: Small mound 65 m E on the lower floodplain ridge. Natural.

candidates.label: M14
candidates.interpretation: Mound 71 m S. Low.

candidates.label: M15
candidates.interpretation: Mound 79 m SSE beside trail. Low.

candidates.label: M16
candidates.interpretation: Mound 89 m SE on floodplain. Natural.

candidates.label: D14
candidates.interpretation: Small pit (2x1.7 m, 0.16 m, 11 pts) 90 m NW on open upper terrace. Probably animal burrow/wallow. Low.

candidates.label: M17
candidates.interpretation: Small mound 104 m SE floodplain. Natural.

candidates.label: D15
candidates.interpretation: Elongated hollow 110 m E on floodplain (scroll swale). Natural.

candidates.label: M18
candidates.interpretation: Small mound 116 m SE floodplain. Natural.

candidates.label: D1
candidates.interpretation: Best cellar/excavation candidate, low-moderate confidence. Steep-sided linear hollow ~7 m N-S x 3-4 m wide, 0.30-0.45 m deep (188 ground pts; raw points confirm), parallel to the house long axis and lying 1-3 m OUTSIDE (west of) the west foundation-stone row along the north half of the house, with a 0.3 m higher bank 4-10 m further west (M2/M3 ridge). Reads like an excavation trench/ backfilled cellar with spoil to the west (e.g. the 1959 NPS dig), or a cellar if the stone row is not the true west wall. Alternatives: entrenched visitor path (Esri trail runs along this wall, although the same trail shows no entrenchment 15-30 m SE), or a stump/root hollow (6 m canopy adjoins on the east). No comparable hollow exists inside the stone outline itself.

dataset.access_note: rockyweb.usgs.gov LAZ download was blocked (TLS reset) from this environment; the identical 3DEP points were read from the public EPT (s3 usgs-lidar-public/ND_SouthWest_1_D21, EPSG:3857) and reprojected to EPSG:26913; Z agrees with the earlier 0.5 m DEM export to median -0.1 cm.
dataset.acquisition: 2021-11-06 ~20:40-21:10 UTC (GPS time), leaf-off; work unit collected 2021-10-29..2021-11-08; 2 flight lines over site (point source IDs 194, 197)
dataset.quality_level: QL2, linear-mode lidar, USGS Lidar Base Spec 2021 rev A; USGS summary report: produced to meet 9.8 cm absolute vertical accuracy at 95% confidence in non-vegetated open terrain (per-project NVA/VVA test values not found in the staged reports)

detectability: Ground returns ~5/m2 (mean spacing ~0.45 m), relative noise ~2.4 cm (std of ground points about a 1.5 m local plane on flat ground). Reliable detection needs >= ~15-20 ground points across a feature and >= ~8-10 cm relief: i.e. hollows/mounds ~2 m or more across and ~0.1 m or more deep/high. Linear berms/hollows ~1-1.5 m wide and >= 10 cm can show if they run > ~5 m. Individual foundation stones, post holes, sill logs and fence lines are NOT resolvable. Cottonwood canopy (leaf-off) did not degrade ground returns at the house (1% empty 1 m cells); grass thatch may lift the ground surface a few cm.

background_rates.note: Tier-A (compact, open, off-scarp) features per hectare of eligible ground

ring_test.method: scripts/08_ring_test.py: rim annulus >=3 cm above interior and outside in N of 12 sectors; exhaustive search house window (80x100 m) vs two equal background windows

corral_ring_R7.5-12.5m.house_window: 2 weak hits (8/12) at +14E,+31N and -16E,+47N (not west of house)

east_scarp: House terrace ~649.0 m. Break of slope begins ~18-24 m E of house center; steepest face (max 21 deg, ~0.9 m drop over ~3 m) at ~33-37 m E; total drop ~2.0 m to a swale at ~646.9 m at 48 m E (possible abandoned channel), low ridge 647.6 m at 55-65 m, then gradual descent to the 2021 river edge ~140 m ESE (cut bank ~1 m, water 643.65 m). 647.8 m contour lies 29-45 m E of house center over +-60 m N-S with no re-entrant notch > 1.5 m (scripts/12_scarp_notch.py).
